note: Evidence levels: TESTED = automated test passes in CI and locally; OS_SANDBOX_CI = additionally exercised under Docker --network none --read-only in CI; DESIGNED = enforced by architecture but not independently demonstrated. None of these is a security or privacy certification.

requirements.requirement: Offline MCP works with network disabled
evidence: TESTED (runtime guard blocks all network APIs)
OS_SANDBOX_CI (docker --network none)

requirements.requirement: Offline MCP works on a read-only filesystem
evidence: TESTED (runtime guard blocks all fs writes)
OS_SANDBOX_CI (docker --read-only, source mounted read-only)
TESTED (zero connection/DNS attempts; no URL literal in source; no WalletWall hostname in bundle)
TESTED (production lockfile scan; bundle imports only node:crypto, node:process)
TESTED (all cwd/HOME/TMP/APPDATA/XDG dirs empty after session; zero fs-write attempts)
TESTED (no files; no cross-request leakage)
TESTED (no randomness or identity API called at runtime; none referenced in source)
TESTED (no os identity API; byte-identical output across separate processes)

requirements.requirement: Wallet addresses not written to disk
evidence: TESTED (unique canary address absent from all files, paths and stderr)
TESTED (no file contains sha256/sha1/md5/sha512 of the canary in hex/base64; no files at all)
TESTED (canary credentials in the environment never appear in files, stderr or responses; source never reads process.env)
TESTED (malformed input survived with no network/files; fatal handler prints one fixed line)
TESTED (tool/resource/source scan; registry schema holds issuers only)
TESTED (count 0 across the whole session; positive control shows the guard counts attempts)
OS_SANDBOX_CI

requirements.requirement: No HTTP/SSE/server transport code is shipped in the runtime artifact
evidence: TESTED (esbuild module graph limited to the SDK stdio server; bundle text has no network, listen, spawn, env, argv, eval or Function primitive; HTTP code REMOVED from the shipped bundle)

requirements.requirement: No listening or connected inet socket during startup, including with hostile environment variables and arguments
evidence: TESTED (OS socket table read from outside the process on Windows and Linux; positive control detects TCP and UDP sockets; zero sockets for source and bundle entries)

requirements.requirement: The Evidence Explorer canvas persists nothing in the browser and its page can talk only to its own loopback origin
evidence: TESTED (Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none' with connect-src 'self'; no storage, cookie, remote URL or dynamic code in the page script; Host and path-key checks; closing the canvas stops the listener and drops the bundle)

requirements.requirement: The combined plugin path (canvas plus MCP) makes zero outbound network connections, zero DNS lookups and zero persistent writes, and opens exactly one loopback listener
evidence: TESTED (canvas profile of the guard records and blocks; positive control; every MCP server the canvas starts runs under the strict guard and reports zero; no files in cwd, HOME, TMP, APPDATA or XDG; canary wallet address, its hashes and canary credentials absent from files and diagnostics)

requirements.requirement: Canvas source contains no filesystem, OS, DNS, raw-socket, TLS, VM, worker, telemetry, identifier-generation or environment-reading code beyond PATH for the MCP child
evidence: TESTED (import allow-list per file; pattern scan; ESLint no-restricted-imports/globals on plugin extension files)

notProven: Behavior of the Copilot client, model provider, Node.js internals or the operating system with respect to user data. GitHub Copilot processes conversation and tool data under GitHub's own product behavior; nothing here claims that data never leaves the machine through Copilot.
Native-code or syscall-level behavior outside the in-process guard (covered only by the Linux CI Docker sandbox and the OS socket-table reader).
Platforms other than the CI runners (Linux, Windows) and the developer machine.
Node.js runtime switches that WalletWall code does not control, for example NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect, which opens a debugger port in any Node process.
How the Copilot app embeds, caches or logs a canvas iframe, and what the app records about canvas actions and results.
